thread:
tanvi: kicking off a follow-up on the tenant quarantine / service splintering idea — long-term refactor to isolate noisy tenants and reduce cross-tenant tail latency. looking for quick tradeoff notes and rollout constraints.

mike: sounds important. what's the primary metric pushing this? is it cost, p99, or operational blast radius?

tanvi: a mix. main drivers: persistent tail latency from hot tenants and the unit-cost increase when we overprovision for worst-case. also safety: some tenants need strict isolation for compliance.

priya: curious about state: sessions, KV, caches. are we duplicating state per-splinter or doing a shared-store with access controls?

sam: quick sketch: prefer per-splinter caches + eventual replicate from central store. dual-write during migration window to avoid synchronous coupling. observability needs to be per-tenant.

arch-bot: RFC (tenant-splintering-v1) posted — https://redwood.internal/rfcs/tenant-splintering-v1 — includes initial diagram and compatibility matrix.

jess: owner question: who owns oncall for a splintered tenant? platform oncall or tenant team? and how do we handle playbooks?

tanvi: proposed ownership: platform owns routing, failover, and infra; splinter (app) owners handle app-level issues. we'll add a small runbook template and automated failback that platform can trigger.

mike: rollback mechanics? need a clear zero-downtime fallback and a way to drain in-flight sessions. also call out tenants that are allowed only on private infra.

tanvi: agree. plan: header-based router -> route to splinter. fallback rule set on router with circuit-breaker TTL. drain policy: stop new sessions, let existing ones finish, then switch. for private-only tenants we tag them and skip splintering.

priya: perf budget for each splinter is critical. otherwise we just move cost and unpredictability around. propose hard qps/leaky-bucket limits per splinter + autoscale caps. :thinking:

sam: +1. I'll draft a playbook with tests: smoke cut, chaos (pod eviction), perf regression, and data consistency checks. will include a small integration test harness.

jess: happy to run a pilot with Tenant-A (low risk) once we have the runbook. can validate latency improvements and observe failback.

tanvi: awesome — thanks. i'll add follow-up tasks to the RFC: migrations, runbook, perf budgets, owners, infra tagging for private tenants. tagging @sam @jess @mike for rough estimates.

mike: estimate: small spike (2w) for routing + tests, migration work depends on number of stateful tenants.

priya: will add checklist for session/KV migration and compliance review.

sam: noted. i'll post a draft playbook by end of week. :thumbsup:

jess: +1. please @mention me when pilot window is open.

tanvi: thanks all — leaving the RFC open for comments, will schedule a 30m sync if folks want to walk the plan together.
